decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice.Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: 531224-111531224-112531224-113531224-121531224-122531224-123531224-124531224-125531224-126Location PlanEnergy Statement Design and Access StatementReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved refuse storage details as set out in  drawing 531224-123 before the development is occupied. The refuse storage shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the developmentReason: To ensure the provision of refuse storage in accordance with the Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (2024).

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including site clearance, demolition and all preparatory work) a scheme for the protection of all retained trees in accordance with BS5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS), and Tree Protection Plans (TPPs), covering each stage of the development. The development shall be carried out in full compliance with the Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plans unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plans shall contain: full details of all aspects of design, site clearance, demolition and construction work with the potential to affect trees, physical measures for the protection of trees, and construction practices, site management and if applicable arboricultural supervision to demonstrate how retained trees will be adequately protected. Plans shall be of legible scale, dimensioned where appropriate. The AMS and TPPs shall include the following information:Details of all facilitation tree worksProvide the siting and design of all aspects of works within the Root Protection Area (RPA), or which otherwise have the potential to affect retained trees, to demonstrate how all aspects of design will prevent damage to trees, including proposed foundations:Location and installation of all drainage and utility services including temporary servicesFull specification for the construction of hard surfacing including existing and proposed ground levels. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) the specification / plan shall demonstrate how it will be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses.Details of all other hard and soft landscaping within RPAs of retained trees.Location and installation of buildings, boundary treatments and ancillary structures, in or close to RPAs.Location and specification of any remediation works.Existing and proposed ground levels.Identify different phases of the works for which a different arrangement of tree protection will be required. For each phase, prepare a Tree Protection Plan to show the following:Location of retained trees (and their post pruning crown spread if applicable).Location of Construction Exclusion Zones.Location of tree protective fencing.Location of ground protection.Location of all works to be undertaken during that phase and construction space for their implementation.Location of site access, parking, loading, unloading, welfare facilities and storage of equipment, materials, fuels, mixing of concrete, applicable to that phase.Provide specification for tree works, protective fencing and ground protection.Identify site preparation and construction practices and site management arrangements to prevent damage to trees. Aspects to include: clearance of vegetation, erection and installation of: buildings and structures, hard surfacing, drainage and utilities, boundary treatments, remediation works, planting, and all other demolition and construction activities.Reason: To protect important landscape features within the site in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990

The development shall not commence until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The Construction Management Plan shall be written in accordance with London Best Practice Guidance and contain:o	A photographic condition survey of the public roads, footways and verges leading to the site;o	Details of construction access and associated traffic management;o	Arrangements for the loading, unloading and turning of o	Delivery, construction and service vehicles;o	Arrangements for the parking of contractors' vehicles;o	Arrangements for wheel cleaning;o	Arrangements for the storage of materials;o	Hours of work;o	The storage and removal of excavation material;o	Measures to reduce danger to cyclists;o	Dust mitigation measures;o	Membership of the Considerate Contractors SchemeThe development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure construction does not lead to damage of the nearby public road network and to minimise disruption to the neighbouring properties.

The outbuilding hereby permitted shall not be occupied at any time other than for purposes ancillary to the residential use of the main dwelling at number 96 Waggon Road and shall not be used as independent self-contained accommodation.Reason: To ensure that the development complies with adopted standards, does not impact on neighbouring amenity and is in character with the existing form of development in the locality in accordance with relevant adopted planning policies of the Enfield Local Plan.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied at any time other than for purposes ancillary to the residential use of the existing dwelling at number 96 Waggon Road and shall not be used as an independent dwelling at any time. Reason: To ensure that the development complies with adopted standards, does not impact on neighbouring amenity and is in character with the existing form of development in the locality in accordance with relevant adopted planning policies of the Enfield Local Plan.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the external materials specified in the approved Design and Access Statement dated February 2025, unless otherwise submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure an appearance which complies with Development Plan Policies.

No above ground works shall commence until details of a landscaping plan detailing trees, shrubs and grass to be planted and the treatment of any hard surfaced amenity areas has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The site shall be landscaped in accordance with the approved details in the first planting season after completion or occupation of the development whichever is the sooner. Any trees or shrubs which die, becomes severely damaged or diseased within five years of planting shall be replaced with new planting in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To provide a satisfactory appearance

The development hereby approved shall be carried out in full accordance with the Energy Statement prepared by L16 Desgins, dated 19 Sep 2025, unless otherwise submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved measures for reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, including but not limited to the use of low and zero carbon technologies, enhanced building fabric performance, and energy-efficient systems, shall be fully implemented prior to first occupation of the development and retained thereafterReason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

Following practical completion of works a final Energy Performance Certificate with accompanying Building Regulations compliance report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where applicable, a Display Energy Certificate shall be submitted within 18 months following first occupation.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The development shall be designed and constructed to ensure that the internal consumption of potable water does not exceed 105 litres per person per day. This shall be achieved through the installation of water-efficient fittings, appliances, and, where applicable, water recycling systems. The development shall be maintained in accordance with these measures for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP21 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policy DMD58 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The glazing to be installed in all first-floor windows on the eastern flank elevation of the development shall be in obscured glass and fixed shut to a height of 1.7m above the floor level of the room to which they relate. The glazing shall not be altered without the approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of adjoining properties.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 1995 or any amending Order, no buildings or extensions to buildings shall be erected without the prior approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interests of residential amenity and to prevent the overdevelopment of the site.

Notwithstanding the submitted plans, prior to first occupation, cycle parking shall be provided in compliance with the following criteriao	Provision of a minimum of TWO long stay cycle parking spaceso	in an accessible location: the access route to the cycle parking enclosures should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike to enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door) which must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2mo	long stay must be secured: with a British Standard mortice lock or access fobo	long stay must be fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roofReason: The Council's Climate Action and Transport Policies seek to increase the use of active and sustainable transport modes. This means that access to bicycle parking should be easy and secure to remove potential barriers to cycling.
